$x + 3y - z = - 18$

$3x - y + \left({λ}^{2} - \left|\lambda\right|\right)z = 16$& has no solutions, is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
For the system of linear equations

$2x - 3y + 5z = 9$

$x + 3y - z = - 18$

$3x - y + \left({λ}^{2} - \left|\lambda\right|\right)z = 16$~to have~no solutions,~

$∆$~should be equal to~$0$.

i.e.~$\Delta = \left|$\begin{cases}2 & - 3 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & - 1 \\ 3 & - 1 & {λ}^{2} - \left|\lambda\right|\end{cases}$\right|$

$= 2\left(3{λ}^{2} - 3 \left|\lambda\right| -1\right) + 3 \left({λ}^{2} - \left|\lambda\right| +3\right) + 5\left(-1 - 9\right)$

$= 9{λ}^{2} - 9\left|\lambda\right| -43$

$= 9\left|\lambda\right|2 - 9\left|\lambda\right| -43$

Now~$∆ = 0$~for~$2$~values of~\left|\lambda\right|$~as for the above quadratic the value of determinant is greater than zero.

So,~$2$~values of~$\lambda$& satisfy the system of equations to obtain no solution.

$

If $\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 2\pi,$~then the system of equations

$x + \left(cos\gamma\right)y + \left(cos\beta\right)z = 0$

\left(cos\gamma\right)x + y + \left(cos\alpha\right)z = 0$

\left(cos\beta\right)x + \left(cos\alpha\right)y + z = 0$

has :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 2\pi$

Now,~$\Delta = \left|$\begin{cases}1 & cos\gamma & cos\beta \\ cos\gamma & 1 & cos\alpha \\ cos\beta & cos\alpha & 1\end{cases}$\right|$

By expanding along the first column, we get

$∆ = 1\left(1 - \cos^{2}\alpha\right) - cos\gamma \left($cos$\gamma -$cos$\alpha .$cos$\beta\right) +$cos$\beta\left($cos$\alpha .$cos$\gamma -$cos$\beta\right)

$∆ = 1 - \cos^{2}$\alpha - \cos^{2}\gamma +$cos$\gamma .$cos$\alpha .$cos$\beta +$cos$\beta .$cos$\alpha .$cos$\gamma - \cos^{2}\beta

$= 1 - \cos^{2}$\alpha - \cos^{2}\beta - \cos^{2}\gamma +$2cos$\alpha .$cos$\beta .$cos$\gamma

$= \sin^{2}$\alpha - \cos^{2}\beta -$cos$\gamma ($cos$\gamma -$2cos$\alpha .$cos$\beta )

$= - \cos ( $\alpha + \beta ) .$\cos ( $\alpha - \beta ) -$cos$\gamma \left[\cos \left\${2\pi - ( \alpha + \beta )\right - $2cos\alpha .cos\beta\right]

$= - \cos ( $2\pi - \gamma )$\cos ( $\alpha - \beta ) --cos\gamma \left[\cos ( \alpha + \beta ) - 2cos\alpha . cos\beta\right]$

$= - \cos ( 2\pi - \gamma ) . \cos ( \alpha - \beta ) - cos\gamma \left[$cos$\alpha .$cos$\beta -$sin$\alpha .$sin$\beta -$2cos$\alpha .$cos$\beta\right]

$= - cos$\gamma .$\cos ( $\alpha - \beta ) +$cos$\gamma .$\cos ( $\alpha - \beta )

$= 0$

So,~$∆ = 0$

Hence, the system of equations has infinitely many solutions.

$

\left|$\begin{cases}x & - 6 & - 1 \\ 2 & - 3x & x - 3 \\ - 3 & 2x & x + 2\end{cases}$\right| = 0,$ \text{ and } is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& \left|$\begin{cases}x & - 6 & - 1 \\ 2 & - 3x & x - 3 \\ - 3 & 2x & x + 2\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

On expansion, we get~$x\left\{- 3x\left(x + 2\right) - 2x\left(x - 3\right)\right\} + 6\left\{2\left(x + 2\right) + 3\left(x - 3\right)\right\} - 1\left(4x - 9x\right) = 0$

$⇒ x\left\{- 3x^{2} - 6x - 2x^{2} + 6x\right\} + 6\left\{2x + 4 + 3x - 9\right\} - 1\left(- 5x\right) = 0$

$⇒ - 5x^{3} + 30x - 30 + 5x = 0$

$⇒ 5x^{3} - 35x + 30 = 0$

$⇒ x^{3} - 7x + 6 = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 1\right)\left(x - 2\right) \left($x + 3\right)$

$⇒ x = 1$~or~$x = 2$~or~$x = - 3 .$

Here all roots \left\{1, 2, - 3\right\}$~are real, hence the sum of the real roots is~$1 + 2 - 3 = 0 .

$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$S$ be the set of all values of $\theta \in [ - \pi, \pi ]$ for which the system of linear equations
$x + y + \sqrt{3}z = 0$
$- x + ( tan\theta ) y + \sqrt{7}z = 0$
$x + y + ( tan\theta ) z = 0$
has non-trivial solution,

So, by condition of non-trivial solution we get,

\left|$\begin{cases}1 & 1 & \sqrt{3} \\ - 1 & tan\theta & \sqrt{7} \\ 1 & 1 & tan\theta\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left(\tan^{2}\theta - \sqrt{7}\right) - \left(- tan\theta - \sqrt{7}\right) + \sqrt{3}\left(- 1 - tan\theta\right) = 0$

$⇒ \tan^{2}\theta + \left(1 - \sqrt{3}\right)tan\theta - \sqrt{3} = 0$

$⇒ \left(tan\theta + 1\right)\left(tan\theta - \sqrt{3}\right) = 0$

$⇒ tan\theta = \sqrt{3}, - 1$

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{π}{3}, \dfrac{- 2\pi}{3}, \dfrac{- \pi}{4}, \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$

Hence,

$\dfrac{120}{π} ∑ \theta = 120\left(\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{2}{3} - \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4}\right) = 20$

$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

System of equations,

$6\lambdax - 3y + 3z = 4{λ}^{2}$

$2x + 6\lambday + 4z = 1$

$3x + 2y + 3\lambdaz = \lambda$

For no solution~$△ = 0$,

So,~\left|$\begin{cases}6\lambda & - 3 & 3 \\ 2 & 6\lambda & 4 \\ 3 & 2 & 3\lambda\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

$⇒ 9{λ}^{3} - 7\lambda - 2 = 0$

$⇒ ( \lambda - 1 ) ( 3\lambda + 1 ) ( 3\lambda + 2 ) = 0$

Hence,~$\lambda \in \left\{1, \dfrac{- 1}{3}, \dfrac{- 2}{3}\right\}$

Now putting the value of~$\lambda$~in~$12\mathop{∑}_{\lambda \in S}\left|\lambda\right|$~we get,

$12\mathop{∑}_{\lambda \in S}\left|\lambda\right| = 12 \times \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3}\right) = 24$
